standard.name: KL OS Standard
standard.description: KL OS Standard with restored KL Store, KL Maker, Files, Browser, Mail, Website Hosting, OS Update and interactive authenticated Remote Desktop. Antivirus with a separately managed, protected security update channel. Includes Security & Privacy Center with local audit, privacy controls and system integrity checks. Includes KL Disk Manager for multiple mounted floppy drives and removable-file storage.

government.name: HackOS Government
government.description: HackOS Government with restored Hack Console, KL Store, KL Maker, Remote Center, interactive multi-PC Remote Desktop, file transfer, power management, Mail and website hosting. Antivirus with a separately managed, protected security update channel. Includes Security & Privacy Center with local audit, privacy controls and system integrity checks. Includes KL Disk Manager and a safe Malware Lab for non-destructive behaviour simulations.

notes.desktop: Windows-inspired desktop with taskbar-only app shortcuts, Start menu, right-click creation context menu, title bars and a taskbar action to return from the current maximised app view. No custom cursor is drawn.
notes.file_execution: Files can launch Lua scripts with CraftOS shell.run; text, config and HTML files open in the built-in CraftOS editor.
notes.updates: OS Update stages and rolls back system files. Documents, website content, mailbox data, user-created apps in /Applications and the installed-app registry are not part of the system file list and are preserved.
notes.websites: Website Studio creates and edits HTML pages under /www. The background rednet website service hosts index.html and other .html files for both KL Browser and HackOS Browser. It supports a simple HTML subset: title, headings, paragraphs, links, lists and line breaks; CSS and JavaScript are not executed.
notes.hosting: Enable hosting in Website Server or Website Studio. The server stays active in the OS background service while you continue to use other apps.
notes.remote_desktop: Authenticated interactive remote desktop for updated KL OS / HackOS computers. The controller receives live terminal frames and forwards keyboard, paste, click, right-click, drag, mouse-up and scroll events. Screen cells are scaled to the controller terminal. CC:Tweaked does not expose a passive mouse-hover event, so pointer position follows clicks/drags rather than free hover.
notes.file_transfer: Remote file transfer is restricted to /public; files are limited to 8192 bytes.
notes.mail: HackOS internal mail uses rednet between reachable computers; it is not external SMTP or Gmail.
notes.recovery: Installer stores recovery copies under /hackos/recovery/files. Deleting a system file triggers a blue-screen-style recovery flow. Press R to restore missing files or run rescue.lua from CraftOS.
notes.exploit_lab: Government includes a deliberately fictional Minecraft-only KLOS-BOOT-OVERWRITE exploit against KL OS Standard system files. It is not a general-purpose exploit.
notes.app_store: KL Store contains offline packages (Calculator, Notes, System Monitor and Dice Roller). Apps install into /Applications, register in the Start menu and are automatically pinned to the taskbar after core shortcuts when display space allows.
notes.maker: KL Maker is a visual component builder. Website projects export HTML into /www; app projects export Lua programs into /Applications and register them in the Start menu. Projects are saved in /Documents/KLMaker.
notes.apps: Custom and Store-installed apps are listed in Start and pinned to the taskbar when space allows. User applications are stored in /Applications; the app registry is /Applications/installed.json.
notes.restored_apps: Government edition includes Hack Console, KL Store and KL Maker. Both editions include KL Store and KL Maker plus Calculator, Notes, System Monitor and Dice Roller packages. App entries and package paths are included in both edition manifests where applicable.
notes.privacy: Security & Privacy Center stores preferences and audit records locally. No analytics or telemetry is transmitted. Users can disable discovery responses, inbound/outbound internal mail, remote administration, guest diagnostics, the KL OS system exploit lab and website hosting; emergency Lockdown turns these exposure points off together. A local integrity scan compares installed system files against the recovery image. It is not malware detection and does not sandbox arbitrary Lua applications.
notes.audit: Security audit log is local-only at /hackos/security/audit.log, bounded to the latest 160 events. It records setting changes, remote authentication outcomes, mail and selected remote actions. It does not record message bodies, access codes or keystrokes.
notes.network_discovery_privacy: Turning off network discovery stops this computer from responding to compatible KL OS / HackOS discovery broadcasts. It does not turn off the modem, block all rednet packets, or prevent access through a known computer ID/IP when another service is enabled.
notes.integrity_scan: Integrity scan compares files named by /hackos/recovery/index.json with local recovery copies. Locally modified system files may be reported; the scanner does not use cryptographic signatures or detect all malicious user files.
notes.exploit_lab_control: The deliberate Government-to-Standard system-file exploit lab is controlled by /hackos/privacy.json exploit_lab. When disabled, SYSTEM_PROBE, SYSTEM_EXPLOIT, SYSTEM_LIST and SYSTEM_DELETE requests are rejected. Default is enabled to preserve the established lab gameplay; Emergency Lockdown disables it.
notes.disk_storage: KL Disk Manager scans all discoverable CC:Tweaked drive peripherals, including peripherals exposed through wired modems when available. Each inserted data floppy is mounted as its own filesystem (disk, disk2, etc.). Files can be copied between floppy mounts and /Documents, /www or /Applications. Drives and floppy capacity are limited by the attached peripherals and Minecraft media; this is not unlimited aggregate storage.
notes.malware_lab: Government-only safe simulator. Scenario files are data-only .klvirus JSON records. Ransomware, wiper, worm and trojan demonstrations alter only virtual sample states in /HackOS-Lab/lab-state.json. No executable malware is generated, no real user/system files are encrypted/deleted, and no propagation packets or persistence are created.
